news.title: Like Eagles, like Falcons: The dwindling fortunes of Africa’s 10-time champions
news.lede: Nigeria’s storied football institutions are stuttering in tandem, with the Super Falcons following the Super Eagles down the painful road of a World Cup play-off, the parallel has become impossible to ignore, PETER AKINBO writes. There is a peculiar heartbreak that visited Nigerian football twice within the space of a year when the Super Eagles lost automatic qualification and again in the play-offs. The pain has arrived again, from an unlikely source. Just as the Super Eagles discovered in November 2025 that automatic qualification was no longer a birthright, the Super Falcons were handed the same delivery barely nine months later, and the coincidence has become too glaring for anyone in Nigerian sport to dismiss as bad luck alone.

news.title: World Cup hero’s $125m Premier League exit on eve of season
news.lede: Manchester City have accepted a £65.4 million ($125 million) bid from Barcelona for their World Cup-winning Spain midfielder Rodri, British media reported. The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner has agreed a four-year deal with the Spanish champions, Sky Sports said, and will head to the Nou Camp to complete the transfer next week. Spain’s Rodri is presented the FIFA World Cup. It comes a week after City knocked back a $75m offer from Barcelona.
